screens_reviewed: Two scroll captures of audit/[placeId]/[step] at step 3 (Access domain): 11-audit-domain.png (top: step header, progress chip, step pills, section intro) and 12-audit-domain-questions.png (mid-scroll: condition follow-up + presence question cards and the absolute footer nav).
verdict: This is the dark-theme capture, yet the entire screen renders the cream/light palette: cream background, white cards, dark-green selected option rows, dark text. The audit wizard imports the static `designSystem` (light) constant instead of the live `useDesignSystem()` hook, so theme switching is dead on this whole route. The layout, hierarchy, and footer are otherwise well built and thumb-reachable, but the broken dark theme is a real, screen-wide correctness bug.

critical_issues.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx top-level import and every component (e.g. YStack bg, StepHeader, Card, SelectionButton, FooterNav)
critical_issues.issue: The screen is captured under the dark theme but renders the light/cream palette (cream #FBFAF6-ish background, white surface cards, dark-green selected rows, dark text). Every style in this file reads from the module-level static `designSystem` constant, which is hard-wired to `lightColors`, so the route never reflects the auditor's dark preference. The rest of the app (header, tab bar, navigation theme in core) uses `useDesignSystem()` and would render dark, leaving this route visibly inconsistent with the surrounding chrome.
critical_issues.evidence: lib/design-system.ts:453-460 (`export const designSystem = { colors: lightColors, ... }`); imported at audit-placeId-step.md (PACK) [step].tsx:23 (`import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system"`) and consumed at [step].tsx:426, 433, getSurveyPalette [step].tsx:1787-1805, getStepTone [step].tsx:1774-1782; visible cream background and white cards in 11-audit-domain.png / 12-audit-domain-questions.png despite the dark capture.
critical_issues.fix: Call `useDesignSystem()` inside `AuditStepScreen` and thread the resolved tokens down (or read it in each child component) instead of importing the static `designSystem`. `getSurveyPalette` / `getStepTone` must take the resolved `colors` as an argument rather than closing over the light constant. This mirrors how core's app/_layout.tsx and (tabs)/_layout.tsx already consume `useDesignSystem()`.

improvements.suggestion: Once dark theme is wired up, re-check the selected option treatment: selected rows use `palette.selected = colors.primary` with `primaryForeground` text. In dark, `primary` is mint green #7FBFA3 and `primaryForeground` is near-black #0E1A16, which is a strong pairing; but verify the unselected `palette.inner = colors.input` (#1B1D19) against `palette.accent = primary` (#7FBFA3) label still reads clearly, since unselected option labels are tinted with the accent green rather than the foreground.
improvements.evidence: [step].tsx:1300-1314 (selected vs inner background, accent label color); lib/design-system.ts:342-375 dark tokens

improvements.location: Card [step].tsx:1072, SelectionButton :1273, ProgressBar in SectionProgressCard :1413-1427, CommentField Input :1339
improvements.suggestion: This route hand-rolls Card, button rows, and a progress track inline while core ships shared `components/ui/Card.tsx`, `Button.tsx` (AppButton), and `ProgressBar.tsx` that already consume `useDesignSystem()`. Adopting the shared primitives (or at least the pattern) would have prevented the static-palette bug and keeps spacing/radii consistent. PACK declares `design_system_components_used: (none)`, confirming nothing shared is used here.
improvements.evidence: PACK line 4 `design_system_components_used: (none)`; core components/ui/Card.tsx:1752, ProgressBar.tsx:2243 all use useDesignSystem()

improvements.suggestion: Option rows use py="$3" (~12pt top+bottom) plus single-line text, yielding roughly a 44pt row at default scale — at the iOS minimum but not generous for a field tool used one-handed. Consider a minHeight tied to layout.formOptionHeight (42 phone) or bumping to py="$3.5" so short labels like "Yes?"/"No?" keep a comfortable target.
improvements.evidence: [step].tsx:1293-1294 (py="$3" px="$3.5"); single-line rows visible in 12-audit-domain-questions.png; lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:806 formOptionHeight 42

tamagui_notes: Static-vs-hook palette is the root cause: lib/design-system.ts:447-460 documents that the static `designSystem` export is light-only and that screens needing live theme switching must use `useDesignSystem()`; this route violates that contract ([step].tsx:23).

getSurveyPalette ([step].tsx:1787-1805) and getStepTone ([step].tsx:1774-1782) are pure functions closing over the light constant, so even fixing the import requires passing `colors` in as a parameter.

Spacing and radii use Tamagui space tokens ($3, $3.5, $4) and the shared radii scale (radii.xl/lg/md/button) consistently — no raw magic numbers in padding here, which is good; the issue is purely the color source.
platform_notes: Safe-area handling is correct: FooterNav reads `insets.bottom` and adds paddingBottom=bottomInset+12 ([step].tsx:1680, insets from useSafeAreaInsets at :87), so the Back/Save/Next bar clears the home indicator. The footer is visible above the bottom edge in both captures.

Top inset: the route relies on the native stack header (useYeeStackHeaderOptions) plus the root Stack contentStyle paddingTop:20 (core app/_layout.tsx:1378); content clears the Dynamic Island in 11-audit-domain.png. The status bar text is dark on the cream header — once dark theme is fixed the StatusBar style (core sets `light` for dark theme, _layout.tsx:1369) will match the now-dark header.

Thumb reach: primary Next CTA sits in the fixed bottom-right footer within easy thumb range; Back/Save/Next are a flex row using layout.screenPaddingHorizontal (phone 15), so they fit edge-to-edge without overflow.
Compact-fit uses lib/responsive-layout via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle and useResponsiveLayout ([step].tsx:24,85,434) rather than fixed widths — phone layout is handled correctly.
not_assessable: Exact contrast ratios of the rendered (incorrectly light) palette against WCAG thresholds — the palette shown is the wrong one, so measuring it is moot; the correct dark pairings (lib/design-system.ts:342-375) are claimed AA in the source comment but not verified here.

Runtime states not shown: isSaving spinner in the Next button, the danger NoticeCard sync-error banner, and the Alert-based incomplete-step confirmation are code paths not captured in these screenshots.
Whether the dark-theme StatusBar/header chrome visually reconciles with the body once the palette bug is fixed (depends on runtime theme, not capturable from these light renders).
score_rationale: A single but screen-wide correctness defect: in the dark capture the entire audit wizard renders the light palette because it imports the static `designSystem` constant instead of `useDesignSystem()` (lib/design-system.ts:453, [step].tsx:23). Layout, safe-area, hierarchy, and thumb reach are all solid, but a route that ignores the user's theme on every surface is a significant, verifiable problem, landing this in the 3-4 band.
